title: SDK transport ops patterns: empirical timeout harness and connection-reuse recipes
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem: SDK customers (Python/TS/Go) observe inconsistent behavior for long-polling/streaming and burst traffic. Root causes include mismatched client timeouts vs server routing latencies, opaque connection reuse heuristics in platform proxies, and poor defaults for keep-alive/probe intervals across languages. We need an empirical harness + recommended presets and examples to make cross-SDK transport behavior predictable and safe for production workloads.

Goal: Deliver a reproducible test harness that measures p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latencies under realistic workload mixes (short sync calls, streaming, large-batched prompts), produce per-language transport presets (timeouts, pool sizes, keepalive intervals, probe thresholds), and ship example code + migration guidance. The PRs should include tests and docs for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible benchmarking harness (documented runbook) that can execute synthetic mixes: 80% short generate, 15% streaming, 5% large-embed and output latency percentiles
Per-language config presets (minimal and conservative) committed to SDK repos and documented in the Console SDK guidance page
Example snippets for graceful streaming reconnects and idempotent retries for partial responses per language
Automated CI job that runs harness nightly against staging and records regressions to the latency dashboard
Performance regressions (>=10% p95) raise a notification to #sdk-reliability with reproduction artifact
tech_notes: Design a harness that drives clients through a realistic mix; include simulated cross-region hops and injected 1% packet loss to emulate flaky networks
Measure both connection-level metrics (TCP/TLS handshakes, socket reuse rates) and application-level (time-to-first-byte for initial token, streaming chunk pace)

Provide conservative defaults: connection_pool_min=2, connection_pool_max=16, idle_reap=45s, keepalive_interval=15s, per-request deadline = base_latency * 3 + 500ms; base_latency derived from p50 from harness

Provide permissive presets for low-latency environments (edge regions) and conservative presets for high-regulation/private deployments (longer deadlines to avoid spuriously aborting long inference requests)

Important trade-offs: lower keepalive intervals reduce TCP half-open/idle termination but add heartbeats cost on constrained devices; larger pools reduce latency at throughput but increase resource usage on client and server side

Streaming ergonomics guidance: prefer small initial read deadlines for early failure detection, then extend deadlines after first chunk received; supply a reusable reconnect token (resume point) for idempotent streaming endpoints
decisions: We will standardize on two presets across SDKs: 'balanced' and 'conservative' rather than many micro-presets to reduce maintenance overhead
Preset values will be documented in Console and surfaced via SDK helpers (e.g., ClientConfig.from_preset('balanced'))
Retry semantics: non-idempotent streaming requests will not be auto-retried by default; SDKs provide opt-in resumable streaming helper
CI: nightly harness against staging cluster will gate SDK release branches for transport regressions beyond specified thresholds
tasks: Build harness: lightweight runner in Go (bin/harness) that spawns synthetic clients for Python/TS/Go and reports percentile metrics
Add telemetry hooks to SDKs: record connection_reuse_rate, socket_open_count, heartbeat_failures and export to the internal metrics endpoint
Implement SDK helper: ClientConfig.presets({balanced,conservative}) in python-ts-go with unit tests
Write migration guide: 'When to change timeouts and pool sizes' with examples for common failure modes
Add example code for graceful streaming reconnect (resume token) for each SDK and include integration test against local mock server
implementation_notes: Python: implement presets in ClientConfig and ensure urllib3/requests pool limits map to connection_pool_max; provide explicit keepalive socket options when running on Linux (SO_KEEPALIVE + TCP_KEEPINTVL)

TypeScript: for node fetch/got users provide an agent factory that sets maxSockets, keepAlive and freeSocketTimeout; for browser users issue guidance to use short application-level timeouts and fallbacks
Go: expose TransportPresets that set IdleConnTimeout, MaxIdleConnsPerHost and EnableKeepAlives; provide example for net/http.Client with custom DialContext that supports probe hooks
Test plan: run harness at 10x scale locally and 2x in staging; validate 99th percentile under load remains within SLOs; capture full tcpdump for failing runs for root cause analysis
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Aggressive defaults could overload platform proxies during spikes. Mitigation: conservative preset for public tenants and feature-flag rollout for balanced preset via Console
Risk: Language-VM differences (GIL, Node event loop) cause different pooling behavior. Mitigation: measure per-language and publish separate expected baseline numbers
Risk: Customers with NAT timeouts (30s) will see connection drops despite keepalive. Mitigation: document NAT-friendly keepalive intervals and provide reconnect helpers for streaming
